compiled_state.title: [debug-everything/Phase L]: Force-push after rebase -> session ends without waiting for CI checks to pass on updated PR
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Incident Overview

In session 2026-05-05 (after bb83-1a98 surfaced the conflict-resolution gap), the post-rebase force-push to PR #52 returned control to the user without polling the PR's CI checks for the updated commit. The previous PR commit had triggered CI runs, but the force-push invalidates those — new CI runs were queued for the rewritten branch HEAD. The session declared completion without confirming any of:

- All required check contexts re-ran for the new HEAD SHA
- The new runs finished
- The new runs passed

If the rebase introduced a regression (e.g., dropped commit's tests no longer covered, cherry-pick conflict marker survived, environment-dependent flakiness), the user discovers it via a failing PR review or a broken merge later — not at session-end.

## Expected Behavior

After any push that changes the PR HEAD (initial create, force-push after rebase, fixup commit, etc.), Phase L should:

1. Capture the new HEAD SHA
2. Poll `gh pr checks <num>` (or `gh pr view <num> --json statusCheckRollup`) until all checks for that SHA reach a terminal state (success / failure / skipped)
3. Report the rollup verdict: green = session complete, red = surface failing checks and either invoke remediation (per existing CI failure path) or stop with the failure visible to the user

This applies to BOTH the initial push (already partially specified in Phase L) AND any subsequent push that updates the PR — because the merge.strategy=pr workflow can produce post-create pushes (rebase-on-conflict, fixup commits during review-resolution, etc.) and each one resets the check baseline.

## Actual Behavior

In the 2026-05-05 session: after `git push --force-with-lease`, the session emitted a "conflicts resolved, PR mergeable" summary based solely on `mergeable=MERGEABLE`. The `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` was acknowledged as policy (CI/required reviews) but not waited on. CI runs for the new HEAD SHA were not polled to terminal state.

## Affected Paths

- plugins/dso/skills/debug-everything/SKILL.md — Phase L Step 2 (Report Completion) and the merge-and-verify sub-agent's exit conditions
- plugins/dso/skills/debug-everything/prompts/phase-10-merge-verify.md — likely owns the post-push polling logic; may only cover initial-create case
- plugins/dso/scripts/merge-to-main-pr.sh — `_phase_poll` already polls CI for an existing PR HEAD; the caller (debug-everything Phase L) needs to invoke this same logic on every push, not only on initial create

## Suggested Fix Direction

1. Extract the post-push CI-poll loop into a standalone shell helper (or reuse `_phase_poll` from merge-to-main-pr.sh) that takes `<pr-number>` + optional `<expected-head-sha>` and polls until terminal state with bounded timeout (default 1800s; configurable via `merge.pr_max_wait_seconds`).
2. Call this helper from BOTH (a) the initial PR-create exit path AND (b) every additional push site in Phase L (rebase-on-conflict, review-resolution fixup, etc.) — so the contract "session does not end with un-polled checks" holds across every PR-mutating action.
3. On failure verdict: surface failing check names + URLs to the user; do NOT silently end the session. Optional: route to the existing `_phase_remediate` autonomous fix loop.

## Related Tickets

- bb83-1a98-a5b8-4d9b — Phase L missing post-PR-create conflict resolution (filed earlier this session). The two bugs share root cause: Phase L treats "pushed code" as session-complete without verifying mergeability + CI-pass on the actual SHA the user will merge.

## Reasoning for Filing as Bug

The 2026-05-05 session demonstrated the gap empirically. CLAUDE.md "Always Do These" rule 1 routes test/CI failures through /dso:fix-bug; if a session ends with an un-polled PR HEAD, a CI failure on that HEAD is invisible at session-close and never enters the bug-fix path automatically. Treating "code pushed" as equivalent to "checks passing" is the same class of premature-completion error CLAUDE.md rule 13 cautions against.
